accepted.title: Division-ring homological independence of retracts in limit groups
accepted.text: Let L be a finitely generated fully residually free group (a limit group), and H≤L a retract, so there is r:L→H with r|_H=id. Is H D_{K[L]}-independent for every field K? For a field K in the coefficient setup, D_{K[L]} denotes the unique epic Hughes-free division ring generated by K[L]. A subgroup H≤L is D_{K[L]}-independent when the natural inclusion-induced map H₁(H;D_{K[L]})→H₁(L;D_{K[L]}) is injective.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 3.4.1, printed p.65 / PDF p.73; Definitions 3.0.2–3.0.4, printed p.36 / PDF p.44.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Limit groups admit the required coefficient division rings for all fields. Ordinary virtual retractions and the already proved Hall property do not say that this particular retract is independent in L itself; free and surface cases are known.
accepted.literature_finding: The source explicitly isolates the retract assertion as conjectural despite proving the Hall property. Current published Hall results and fresh exact-topic retrieval supply no general retract theorem for all limit groups/all fields.

accepted.title: Free-product closure for residually finite L²-Hall groups
accepted.text: If A and B are finitely generated residually finite L²-Hall groups, must A*B be L²-Hall? A group J is L²-Hall if every finitely generated U≤J lies in a finite-index J₀≤J such that the kernel of H₁(U;N(J₀))→H₁(J₀;N(J₀)) has zero von Neumann dimension; N(J₀) is the group von Neumann algebra.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Question 3.4.3, printed p.65 / PDF p.73; Definition 1.3.1, printed p.4 / PDF p.12.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Residual finiteness and finite generation are retained. Do not substitute subgroup separability, for which a closure theorem already exists. Literal injection is replaced by the actual zero-von-Neumann-dimension kernel condition in the general L² definition.
accepted.literature_finding: The published paper explicitly leaves the residually finite case unclear and gives a non-residually-finite counterexample. That counterexample does not meet the source hypotheses. No later closure result located.

accepted.title: Positive-characteristic failure of the L²-Hall property
accepted.text: Does there exist an L²-Hall group G and a field K of positive characteristic for which D_{K[G]} is defined but G is not D_{K[G]}-Hall? A group J is L²-Hall if every finitely generated U≤J lies in a finite-index J₀≤J such that the kernel of H₁(U;N(J₀))→H₁(J₀;N(J₀)) has zero von Neumann dimension; N(J₀) is the group von Neumann algebra. For a field K in the coefficient setup, D_{K[G]} denotes the unique epic Hughes-free division ring generated by K[G]. A subgroup H≤G is D_{K[G]}-independent when the natural inclusion-induced map H₁(H;D_{K[G]})→H₁(G;D_{K[G]}) is injective. G is D_{K[G]}-Hall when every finitely generated subgroup H≤G is contained in a finite-index G₀≤G in which H is independent in this sense; coefficient extension to the ambient division ring gives the same condition.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Question 3.4.5, printed p.66 / PDF p.74; Definitions 1.3.1 and 3.0.2–3.0.4, printed pp.4,36 / PDF pp.12,44.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: The explicit existence of the coefficient ring only states the defining domain; undefined invariants are not counted as negative examples. This asks a Hall-property separation for groups, unlike the subgroup-level independence transfer in Question 3.4.6.
accepted.literature_finding: The thesis asks this coefficient separation. Current examples prove equality in specific hierarchical families; fresh exact-topic and author checks locate no general witness or impossibility result.

accepted.title: Field independence of division-ring homological subgroup independence
accepted.text: Let H≤G be finitely generated, and let K₁,K₂ be fields for which the Hughes-free coefficient rings D_{K₁[G]} and D_{K₂[G]} exist. If H is D_{K₁[G]}-independent in G, must it be D_{K₂[G]}-independent? For a field K in the coefficient setup, D_{K[G]} denotes the unique epic Hughes-free division ring generated by K[G]. A subgroup H≤G is D_{K[G]}-independent when the natural inclusion-induced map H₁(H;D_{K[G]})→H₁(G;D_{K[G]}) is injective.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Question 3.4.6, printed p.66 / PDF p.74; Definition 3.0.2, printed p.36 / PDF p.44.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Quantifying pairs of fields in the invariant’s defining domain spells out some field versus every field. This does not prove or assume coefficient-ring existence in otherwise undefined settings. The subgroup embedding H≤G is fixed, and independence is not a purely abstract property of H.
accepted.literature_finding: The source says even the free-group case is open beyond the known F₂-versus-Q comparison. Current Hall results for named families and fresh coefficient-independence retrieval provide no all-field comparison theorem.

accepted.title: The L²-Hall and strengthened Hanna Neumann properties for finite abelian hierarchies
accepted.text: Define C₀={1}. Inductively, C_{j+1} consists of groups virtually in C_j and groups obtained as HNN extensions H*_A or amalgams H*_A K with H,K∈C_j and A finitely generated free abelian. Let G lie in some C_j and be torsion-free and hyperbolic relative to virtually abelian subgroups. Must G be L²-Hall and satisfy the strengthened Hanna Neumann inequality Σ_{t∈U\G/V} χ̄(U∩tVt⁻¹)≤χ̄(U)χ̄(V) for every finitely generated U,V≤G? Here χ̄(J)=max{−χ(J),0} is reduced Euler characteristic. A group J is L²-Hall if every finitely generated U≤J lies in a finite-index J₀≤J such that the kernel of H₁(U;N(J₀))→H₁(J₀;N(J₀)) has zero von Neumann dimension; N(J₀) is the group von Neumann algebra.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 3.4.8 and hierarchy Definition 3.4.7, printed p.66 / PDF p.74. Published counterpart Conjecture 1.3.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Read the recursive finite-hierarchy definition and all geometric hypotheses. This enlarges the proved classes of limit groups and graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups. The two conclusions are kept together; the incomplete citation fragment is merged rather than separately numbered.
accepted.literature_finding: Retained in published Conjecture 1.3. Theorems for limit groups and cyclic-edge graphs are proper subcases; current author and exact-topic checks locate no full finite-abelian-hierarchy theorem.

accepted.title: Finite-group word measures determine the free-group automorphism orbit
accepted.text: Let F be free on a finite basis x₁,…,x_d and u,w∈F. For a finite group A, a word v defines v_A:A^d→A by substitution. Suppose |u_A⁻¹(a)|=|w_A⁻¹(a)| for every finite A and a∈A. Must there exist φ∈Aut(F) with u=φ(w)?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 4.1.1, printed p.69 / PDF p.77; repeated discussion printed p.90 / PDF p.98.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Measure equivalence is equality of fibers of word maps, not measured-group orbit equivalence. The automorphism sends the actual word, not merely its generated cyclic subgroup. Primitive and surface-word cases are known, not the arbitrary-word assertion.
accepted.literature_finding: The current prosolvable-rigidity paper retains the general conjecture, and February 2026 Subgroup measures and profinite rigidity in free groups still states it while extending the framework to subgroups. No general closure located.

accepted.title: Profinite rigidity of doubles among cyclic-edge graphs of free groups
accepted.text: Let F be a finitely generated free group and u∈F, and let D_u=F*_{⟨u⟩}F be the double formed by identifying corresponding copies of ⟨u⟩. If H is the fundamental group of a finite graph of finitely generated free groups with cyclic edge groups and Ĥ≅D̂_u, must H≅D_u?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.citation: Question 4.8.1, printed p.90 / PDF p.98; corresponding double construction discussed in §4.6.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: This is unmarked isomorphism of groups from their profinite completions in the specified graph-of-groups comparison class. It does not ask that the amalgamating word be recovered up to an oriented Aut(F)-orbit. When u=1 the edge subgroup is trivial, which is a cyclic allowed boundary case.
accepted.literature_finding: The source retains this general double recognition question. Published surface recognition and 2026 free-factor detection results concern narrower words or additional structure; no full arbitrary-double recognition theorem located.

accepted.title: Parafree Mel’nikov groups are free
accepted.text: Let G be parafree and suppose every finite-index subgroup of G is a one-relator group. Must G be free? Parafree means that G is residually nilpotent and has the same lower-central-series quotients as some free group; one-relator means a finite presentation with one defining relation.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: The finite-index condition includes G itself, so it already entails finite generation. Do not add or remove the Mel’nikov condition, replace parafree by parasurface, or confuse this classification with Fisher’s H₂-vanishing/coherence conjectures.
accepted.literature_finding: The source proves the parasurface case but explicitly leaves the parafree case. Current parafree results do not supply this all-finite-index one-relator classification. It is related to existing Q2722 but has a narrower hypothesis and a sharper free conclusion.

accepted.title: Virtual nonzero second Betti number in one-relator groups
accepted.text: Classify the one-relator groups G for which some finite-index subgroup H≤G has b₂(H)=dim_Q H₂(H;Q)>0. In particular, does every one-ended hyperbolic one-relator group have such a finite-index subgroup?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: The Betti number is ordinary rational second homology, not b₂^(2) or a mod-p invariant. The source contains the full classification question and an explicit named-family subquestion; both are retained in one entry.
accepted.literature_finding: The prosolvable-rigidity result uses virtual nonzero second homology as an additional hypothesis rather than proving it in all groups. Current two-dimensional L²/coherence theorems concern a different invariant, and no full classification or general named-family theorem was located.

accepted.title: Virtual positive second homology of one-ended hyperbolic special groups
accepted.text: Must every one-ended hyperbolic special group G have a finite-index subgroup H≤G with b₂(H)=dim_Q H₂(H;Q)>0? Special means the fundamental group of a special nonpositively curved cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: One-endedness, hyperbolicity and specialness are all retained. Ordinary rational homology is essential. This is a universal assertion for a geometric family, unlike the preceding classification for all one-relator groups; they are not identical classes or conclusions.
accepted.literature_finding: The thesis explicitly proposes this virtual-homology assertion. Current L²-coherence and profinite recognition theorems do not establish it, and exact-topic searches yielded no full theorem or counterexample.

excluded.title: Absolute profinite rigidity of free and surface groups
excluded.text: Let S be a finitely generated free group or the fundamental group of a closed connected surface. For every finitely generated residually finite group H, must an isomorphism of profinite completions Ĥ≅Ŝ imply H≅S?
excluded.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
excluded.citation: Question 1.4.2, printed p.6 / PDF p.14; profinite-rigidity definition immediately above.

locator.verified_from: held physical PDF and printed footer

excluded.scope_review: The comparison class is all finitely generated residually finite groups, not only graphs of free groups, limit groups or one-relator groups. The free and closed-surface branches are preserved together, as in the source. Profinite completions are not bare lists of maps induced by a given homomorphism.
excluded.literature_finding: Current author papers retain absolute rigidity as a central question and prove restricted recognition results. The 2026 Grothendieck-pair and free-factor papers treat additional data/classes, not this unrestricted recognition theorem. No exact later closure located.
excluded.reason: Morales: same absolute profinite rigidity of f.g. free and closed hyperbolic surface groups. Nonhyperbolic surface cases are known and do not add a new open target.

The displayed free-group Strengthened Hanna Neumann Conjecture is already proved by Mineyev and Friedman, as the source expressly states; broader generalizations elsewhere are not this literal statement. The extractor also split the final label digit from Conjecture 1.1.2 or 3.0.1.

The displayed free-group Strengthened Hanna Neumann Conjecture is already proved by Mineyev and Friedman, as the source expressly states; broader generalizations elsewhere are not this literal statement. The extractor also split the final label digit from Conjecture 1.1.2 or 3.0.1.
The source immediately states that Bridson–Grunewald (2004) supplied counterexamples to this full Grothendieck homomorphism question. It is historical motivation, not an unresolved statement.
This is a prose fragment saying the conjecture holds for hyperbolic limit groups, citing a proved theorem. It is not a newly stated Conjecture 3.0.
A prose reference to Conjecture 3.4.8 was extracted as a separate Conjecture 3.4. It supplies no additional assertion; merged into the complete finite-abelian-hierarchy statement.

The mislabeled fragment actually describes Conjecture 4.1.1 about word measures, already reviewed from its complete source statement. Merged as a repeated source discussion, not a second Mel’nikov statement.
Exact Mel’nikov conjecture already appears as Q2722, even though the source identity and cited author differ. The stated two-generator and homology subcases do not warrant a new full-target entry.

The candidate asks for hyperbolic Hall groups outside a virtual finite cyclic hierarchy, but the terminal groups and finite-extension convention of that hierarchy are not explicitly defined in the inspected passage. The finite abelian hierarchy is explicitly defined separately. Hold pending exact cyclic-hierarchy setup rather than imposing a conventional but potentially different terminal class.

The question starts with a finite-index subgroup having the coefficient Hall property and asks about G. Its general coefficient-ring domain for the overgroup, especially beyond local indicability, needs explicit reconciliation with the source’s ordinary L² extension. Do not silently assume existence of D_{K[G]} solely from the subgroup’s property or restrict to the already proved two-dimensional case.

The literal unmarked double D(u) is unchanged when u is replaced by u⁻¹, while the requested conclusion is equality of oriented-word Aut(F)-orbits. An inversion/orientation audit is necessary before promotion. This review does not claim a particular chiral-word counterexample without a verified witness and does not silently weaken the conclusion to cyclic-subgroup equivalence.
